correctness.rationale: Exact tridiagonal path recurrence and the Laurent-substitution root valuation give a zero-root multiplicity m=2^(v2(n+1)+1) exactly for 3|(n+1). The path adjacency has a cyclic vector e1, so its zero-primary sector is one length-m Jordan block. The invertible change of ladder row coordinates yields multiplication by t+epsilon on Fq[t,epsilon]/(t^m,epsilon^2); m is a power of two, so the change z=t+epsilon identifies precisely two length-m blocks. Fitting decomposition then proves the sharp all-parameter entrance counts. Exact independent matrix ranks checked 525 cases n<=84, and exhaustive graph simulations checked 5456 labelled states n<=6. The tests are finite corroboration; the proof is infinite.

value.rationale: The complete two-layer strip is a canonical bounded-degree graph family, and synchronous parity is a canonical local dynamics. The theorem resolves for every length and every finite characteristic-two field the sharp reversibility boundary, nilpotent decomposition and exact transient profile. Distinct mod-three and two-adic arithmetic control an unbounded clock; the striking last-layer proportion 1-q^(-2) persists even when graph length grows. It is not implied by known path or generic finite-field dynamics without the substantial graph-specific Jordan coupling argument.
